bar_narrative: Bar word: slick (owner). From journey J1, on the frozen real-data record (the A3 ring design, 77 parts-list lines): the owner types localhost:8790 in Chrome. Home shows the black ring on white, turning slowly, with its key numbers (30 x 20 x 9.5 mm, 135 mAh, the weight from the mass estimate, 27 hours estimated against the 10-hour target, 8 GB) and eight area tiles, each with one state word. He drags the ring and it turns. He clicks the tile Inside: the ring stays on the stage and a slider 'Closed ... Open it up' appears. He drags it: cover glass, screen, circuit board, cell and housing separate into layers. He clicks the cell: it lights up and the card on the right reads 'Battery cell', what it does and why it is there, then 4.6 x 13.0 x 25.0 mm, 135 mAh minimum, custom order, 'Open: quote from Grepow' (BT1, evidence: calculated). He clicks 'source': the architecture note or the cell datasheet opens in a new tab; a source that is not on disk is greyed with 'not on disk'. If the data was never built, every screen says 'Not built yet. Run npm run collect.'

data_model_notes: No database and no app state (DATA-MAP state-home: none). The data model is the generated bundle under explorer/public/data/ (gitignored, rebuildable), one file per DATA-MAP row, frozen as JSON Schema in explorer/contract/schema/ and as types in explorer/src/contract/ by the contract lane before any other lane starts. Records -> DATA-MAP rows: ring-model -> exterior.glb + internals.glb (row 9); part-placements -> placements.json (row 10); parts -> parts.json (row 11, ring + case lines); part-notes -> explorer/content/part-notes.json (row 12, hand-written, the only non-generated record); key-numbers -> facts.json (row 13); area-states -> areas.json (row 14); look-options -> looks/ (row 15); blocks -> blocks.json (row 16); schematic-pages -> schematic/ (row 17); board-files -> board/ (row 18); firmware-rules -> behaviour.json (row 19); case-model/facts/parts -> case/ (row 20); open-items/decisions -> open.json (row 21); files -> files.json + bundle.zip (row 22). Plus manifest.json and screens.json (screen geometry and states, a derived part of ring-model). Invariants: (1) LINES vs PARTS: a line is one bom.csv row, parts = sum of quantity; '77 lines, 146 parts' on the fixture, and every screen uses these two words with these meanings. (2) part id '<bom>:<ref>', refs split from the reference cell; one ref belongs to exactly one line. (3) every value carries its source {file, line}; no value without one. (4) a record's status is one of ok | missing | unparsed | stale; a failing extractor never stops the run. (5) the app never computes a ring fact: it renders bundle values. (6) design files win over the bundle; deleting public/data and running npm run collect rebuilds it byte-identically for an unchanged source. Two deltas against the owner-checked DATA-MAP, shown to the owner first (gap G5): blocks are created from the schematic sheets and cross-sheet nets instead of architecture section 1; part-notes entries gain model_names[] (the link from 3D objects to parts-list lines, since placement.csv has no reference column). Consumers by path (all to be created): explorer/src/routes/<route>/ for the 9 routes, explorer/src/components/PartCard/, explorer/src/stage/, explorer/src/engine/behaviour/, explorer/tests/** and explorer/journeys/**. No existing consumer: the explorer folder holds only docs/.
